title: Vander Waals Forces, Molecular Solids and Hydrogen Bonding
notes: **Vander Waals forces:** weak intermolecular attractions including London dispersion forces (instantaneous dipoles), dipole-dipole forces (permanent dipoles), and dipole-induced dipole forces.
**London forces:** present in all molecules, strongest in large polarizable molecules. They explain why non-polar substances like $I_2$ and noble gases can condense into liquids and solids.
**Molecular solids:** held together by Vander Waals forces or hydrogen bonds. They have low melting points, are poor conductors, and are often volatile.

**Hydrogen bond:** a strong Vander Waals force between a hydrogen atom bonded to N, O, or F and a lone pair on N, O, or F of another molecule. Much stronger than ordinary Vander Waals forces but weaker than covalent bonds.

**Effects of hydrogen bonding:** water has unusually high boiling point, ice is less dense than liquid water, proteins and DNA have specific 3D structures, and cellulose fibres have high tensile strength.
